**Finding: deviation (high severity) — EXCLUSIVITY**

Two clauses impose de facto exclusivity on us:

- **§ 7.2 (p0026)** — "Before engaging another provider, Customer must disclose and match for Vendor any more favourable commercial offer it receives." This is a right of first refusal that gates our ability to source elsewhere.
- **§ 2.1 (p0012)** — USD 2,000,000/year take-or-pay for three years "without reduction or termination rights," i.e. full-term lock-in with no performance-based exit (walk-away territory).

Both also contradict **§ 12.3**, which recites that Customer gave no exclusivity, MFC, or minimum-volume commitment — that clause is favourable to us and is preserved untouched.

**Redline (validated, preferred level):** delete § 7.2 and replace § 2.1 with a non-exclusive provider statement in which any minimum applies only as expressly stated in a signed Order Form, creates no sole-source obligation, and is reducible/terminable on Vendor's service-level or delivery failure — with the fallback (Order Form volume commitment tied to performance) flagged in the comment.
